custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create two inactive parts for this test, part A and part B.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Make sure no Cycle count is running on the Inventory list.
  • Make sure the app is in the Light theme.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1600 pixels wide with the page zoom at 100%, so the screen is as wide as the design boards.
  • Open the attached design picture of board 4.7 at 100% zoom, so you can compare the screen with it.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Inactive tab.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C839465-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C839465-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • To set a part inactive: on the Inventory page's Active tab click Search, type its part number, click its row; in Edit Inventory Part click Inactive under Part Status, click Save, then click Deactivate in the Deactivate part? window. The part then shows on the Inactive tab.
  • Theme: click your avatar (the AS circle) at the top right; Light and Dark are at the bottom of its menu.
  • A cycle count is running when the Inventory list shows a Count column with Save and Cancel above it; click Cancel to stop it.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A and B are listed on the Inactive tab.

Step 2:

  • The menu opens.

Step 3:

  • The dark bar appears with a blue Activate button.

Step 4:

  • Part A is ticked.

Step 5:

  • Part B is ticked and the badge reads 2.

Step 6:

  • A white dialog opens in the middle of the dimmed page, titled "Activate parts?" in large bold text.
  • The lines read, in this order: "2 parts selected.", "These parts can be added to new work again.", "Existing records that use them stay as they are." (a little bolder).
  • There are exactly three lines: no grey "Stock, cost of goods …" line.
  • A "Note (Optional)" box follows, then a white Cancel and a blue "Activate" button at the bottom right.

Step 7:

  • The dialog closes and parts A and B are still ticked on the Inactive tab: nothing changed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S10-R3: “Raised from the bulk bar, the confirmation is titled "Deactivate parts?" or "Activate parts?". Raised from the part dialog, it is titled "Deactivate part?" or "Activate part?".”
  • S10-R4: “Raised from the bulk bar, the confirmation opens with "{n} parts selected.", or "1 part selected." for one. Raised from the part dialog, it opens with the part number followed by the description, as they stand in the form, with spaces before and after removed.”
  • S10-R8: “For a reactivation from the bulk bar, the confirmation states "These parts can be added to new work again." ("This part ..." for one), followed by "Existing records that use them stay as they are." ("... that use it ..." for one).”
  • S10-R9: “The "Existing records that use ..." line is medium weight. The "Stock, cost of goods and QuickBooks aren't affected." line is grey. Every other line is regular weight in the default text color.”
  • S10-R10: “The confirmation has a note field labelled "Note (Optional)". It stops accepting input at 255 characters.”
  • S10-R11: “The confirm button reads "Deactivate" in red for a deactivation and "Activate" in blue for a reactivation. Cancel sits to its left.”
  • S10-N1: “If the user cancels the confirmation, no part changes status.”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "4.7 Confirm the reactivation". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above where the PRD speaks, and from the board pictures where it is silent about the look.

The design also draws a grey close X at the right end of this confirmation's title row. Product confirmed on 27 Oct 2026 (answer 19) that the X stays and does what Cancel does (PRD v35, Key Decisions and S10-R11a); it is checked by the design case "Design: Status confirmation has a close X in its title row", so this case does not check it.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • bulk-07-p4-7-activate-confirm.png

The design's own words:

  • “"Activate parts?", "2 parts selected.", "These parts can be added to new work again." and "Existing records that use them stay as they are." (S10-R8). The Activate button is blue. On confirm the parts leave the Inactive tab (S3-R4).”
